text: Star Knives (Japanese: , Sutānaifu) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are twin blades wielded by Fiora.

This quest will expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. Starlight Seeker (Japanese: , Kagayaki wo sono Chiisana Te ni) is a Timed Quest in . It can be received from Elior in Alcamoth, northeast of the Fountain of Eternity, near the central teleport pad. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment.

Stopping the Elopement (Japanese: , Tōhikō no Soshi) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Don Argentis in Colony 6 and need 4 stars to be available. If Sharla is in the active party, she will comment. Sharla does not need to be in the active party to accept this quest, but must be the party leader to complete each of the objectives. Completing it unlocks Sharla's Affection skill tree. This quest involving En Argentis is mutually exclusive with Stopping the Elopement involving Zel Argentis. Which one is offered depends on whether Zel Argentis or En Argentis was invited to Colony 6.

This quest will expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. Starlight Gazer (Japanese: , Saranaru Kagayaku wo sono Te ni) is a Timed Quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Elior in Alcamoth, northeast of the Fountain of Eternity, near the central teleport pad, after Starlight Seeker is completed. If Riki is in the active party, he will comment. Upon accepting the quest, the party receives Miriall's Telescope from Elior. After the telescope is upgraded by Kaleka, it becomes the Stronger Telescope.

Spirit - Gadolt (Japanese: , Shinentai Gado) is a story exclusive enemy in . It is a Spirit that can be fought at level 78 near the Moon in Memory Space. It is the last enemy which can be fought before the final battle of the game. Spirit - Gadolt appears as a translucent green version of Jade Face. It is a minor enemy, and thus fighting it is optional. Like all enemies in Memory Space, Spirit - Gadolt drops no Treasure Chests and carries no items which can be stolen. ※ Spirit - Gadolt will respawn after some time, but Memory Space cannot be visited during normal gameplay.

Steel Obart Claws are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by Obart Obarts on Prison Island. Steel Obart Claws are otherwise not available. According to their description, they can cut through anything and are strong enough to cut steel as if it were paper.
Strength of Heart (Japanese: , Mamoru tame no Tatakai, Fight in order to Protect) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located at the Main Entrance of Colony 6, between Shulk and Dunban at pink affinity.

Striker (known as Assault in the Japanese version) is a Class featured in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is one of three classes that can be changed from Drifter. The Striker is specialised in offensive and defensive Arts types. This class grants HP and melee attack bonuses. The basic equipped Weapons are Longsword and Assault Rifle. Once the Class Rank reaches 10, it gives access to the specialised Samurai Gunner or Shield Trooper. The basic Arts of the Striker are Rising Blade, Defensive Stance and Power Dive. Striker has only one Skill slot, the lowest of any class.

Squads were a former mechanic in Xenoblade Chronicles X. A Squad was a team of players who are BLADE members. A Squad could be formed for single player or online multiplayer by recruiting some players connected to the Network across Mira or in the BLADE's Home. With the shutdown of Wii U online services, the mechanic has been discontinued. While playing connected to the Internet, it was possible to participate in a Squad team of up to 32 people. The members who participated in the same Squad would know a free and gradual evolution of relationships and a strengthening of the Squad, the BLADE Reports carried out by each other could be read, and it was possible to cooperate in battle. Squallo, the Sand Mirer (Japanese: , Ryūsa no Sukuāro) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a giant member of the Sabula family. It can be found at level 65 in Oblivia, south of Big Arch, during the day. When the area loads, Squallo briefly rises out of the ground, before returning underground, and will not reemerge until approached.
Star Ciniculas (Japanese: , Sutā Vasaruto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Cinicula family, and can be found at level 20 in Qing Long Glade and Fukai Pass in Noctilum.

Stones are common materials designed for Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be obtained by using Riki's Yoink! ability on the two Berserk Arduns which usually accompany Trainer Harmelon. Sureny Telethia does carry Stones but they are impossible to steal from it.

Stream Jaculs (Japanese: , Sutorīmu Hasutara) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Jacul family, and can be found at level 64-65 above an island in Sylvalum Waters, northwest of FN Site 404, during the day.

Storm Scintimures (Japanese: , Sutōmu Torizumo) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Scintimure family, and can be found at level 41-50 during electromagnetic storms, near the Forgotten Mining Frigates above the Ruined City of O'rrh Sim and Abandoned Bivouac in Cauldros.

Strike Barrager Zigs (Japanese: , Atakkubaretto Jigu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Zig machines, and can be found at level 31-40 on the mountain ledges overlooking Milligan Supply Base in Oblivia.

Starlight Kick (Japanese: , Sutāraito Nī, Lit. "Starlight Knee") is one of Melia's physical arts in and . If used after Spear Break, the enemy will be forcibly Toppled. As Melia uses Starlight Kick, she briefly tumbles onto and stays on the ground.

Spirit Crucible Elpys (Japanese: , Erupisu Reidō) is an area in . It lies within the central Titan of the Leftherian Archipelago, that resides within the great cloud barrier and forms the very center of the archipelago, and is only accessible from the Village Guardian on Fonsett Island, and a Leftherian is needed to open the entrance. The lack of Ether in the air inside the Titan weakens Blades, with the glowing particles in the air absorbing ether, preventing Max Affinity to be reached and for Blade Specials higher than level 1 to be charged. This effect does not apply to artificial Blades such as the various forms of Poppi, including Poppibuster, as well as to Shulk, Fiora, and Elma, who a
The Stomach (Japanese: , Fukubu) of Uraya is a level in . It is located within the Kingdom of Uraya, beyond the Head. Fonsa Myma, the capital city of the Kingdom, is located in the Stomach.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Steam Belts (Japanese: , Suchīmu Beruto) are accessories in and . They increase the wearer's Strength stat by up to 22%. The Silver Belt, Ceramic Belt and Beast-Hide Vest accessories offer stronger instances of this equipment's effect. For a similar additive effect that can stack with this gear, check the Muscle Belt and Champion Belt accessories.

Stranded Merchant (Japanese: , Sōnansha no Kyūshutsu) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Gormott Province, and is unlocked automatically when Garfont Mercenaries reaches Merc Level 3 and the nation reaches 3 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 1 hour, but it can be reduced down to 15 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Botany", "Justice-Loving Soul" and "Leaping" Field Skills.
Star-Crossed Lovers is a quest in . It is automatically received when approaching Norman and Rhiannon on Melnath's Shoulder in Gormott Province.

Street Patrols is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Empire of Mor Ardain, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 4 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 100 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 25 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Dark Mastery", "Water Mastery" and "One Lucky Gal" Field Skills.

Spooky Spirits is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Empire of Mor Ardain by talking to Josie on the bridge above Admar Storage Zone, when the nation has 5 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 2 hours, but it can be reduced down to 30 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Miasma Dispersal" and "Light Mastery" Field Skills.

Strath is an NPC in . He is a Leftherian who can be found on Fonsett Island in the Leftherian Archipelago. He gives the DLC quest Cleared of All Charges upon installing the New Quests Pack 2 of the Expansion Pass.

Stage Star is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Uraya during the Blade Quest Bearing Her Soul, after Ursula obtains 1,500 fans. The time required to complete this mission is 30 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 7 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Fire Mastery" and "Wind Mastery" Field Skills. It rewards stamps that are necessary to level up Ursula's attributes. It also increases Ursula's fanbase by a significant amount.
Star Maples are Flower collectible items in . They can be found in the Kingdom of Torna.
Strength in Unity (Japanese: , Risō no Sekai, Ideal World) is a Quiet Moment in . It is located in the Zekr Marga Quarry on the Bionis' Shoulder, between Shulk and Nene, at any time.

Staying Power (Japanese: , Rimeinfōsu) is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Stalker class. It becomes a usable Master Art upon unlocking the class. Upon use, it sets a field granting Art Follow-Up, a field-exclusive Status Effect which deals 200% of user's Attack as damage to an enemy whenever anyone in the field uses an Art against them.
|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Star Anklets are Accessories in . The common variant can be purchased from the Illicit Caravan. The legendary variant can be acquired by defeating Blazing Karlos.
Squood Fossils are Fossil Collectibles in . They can be found on the Black Mountains. They are fossilized Squoods.

Strategy Manual, vol. 20 is an Accessory in . It grants the user Nia's Salvation's Ripple Chain Order completion bonus and Cammuravi's Heroic Chain when in a Chain Attack. It can be obtained from a Relic to the right of the Prison Island Camp.
Standard Decorations are items in . They can only be dropped by Igruna Standards in Black Mountains.

Strong Screws (Japanese: , Hāto Neji, Heart Screw) are collectables in . They can be found in Prison Island. According to their description, they are blue heart-shaped screws that are small and cute but hard to handle.

Sweet Wasabis (Japanese: , Ama Ama Wasabi) are collectables in . They can be found in Colony 9. According to their description, they are strange spicy-sweet green wasabis that look quite normal otherwise. They are Kino's favorite food according to the Quiet Moment "Power of Imagination" and the post-battle dialogue between him, Shulk, and Melia.

Summon Aqua (Japanese: , Samon Akua) is one of Melia's summon arts in and . It grants the Regenerate buff to Melia and allies within 20 meters, restoring some HP every 3 seconds while the element is active. If two or three aqua elements are active, their effects are added together. When the aqua element is discharged, Melia absorbs some of the target's HP.
Subterranean Zomar (Japanese: , Chitei no Tsumogiri) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Kromar family, and can be found at level 40 at the Soltnar Seal Island in the Eryth Sea.

Suids (Japanese: , Zūsu; English dub: ) are large, pig-like enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Found at the earliest just outside West Gate Plain. Since their arrival on the planet, the Prone have domesticated some suids as warbeasts, adorning them with battle armor. These domestic suids can often be seen at Prone camps, such as Seaswept Base in Primordia. As mentioned in the Affinity Mission One Big Happy Family, Kato's Smile Pizza restaurant in the Commercial District sources its pepperoni from suid meat hunted from wild herds on the plains of Primordia near New Los Angeles.

The Strong Lubricant Oil is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is dropped by the Bright Wisp, which only appears on cloudy nights on Digit 3 during Power Up!. It was probably originally intended to be an objective for that quest.

Strontium Xe-doms (Japanese: , Sutoron Ze-raa) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Xe-dom machines, and can be found in various places in Cauldros, such as the Kw'arah Cloister (level 51 and 55), Ruined City of O'rrh Sim (51-52), and on the slopes of Mount M'gando (both 58-60). With the exception of one in the Kw'arah Cloister, they are dormant until approached.

Sven, the Sturdy (, Kenrō no Suben) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Forfex family. It can be found at level 59 southwest of Primordia, almost directly south of FN Site 217, on a small island in the NLA Waters. Sven, the Sturdy has two notable characteristics: its left claw is missing, and it has 100 resistance to all attack attributes, effectively taking 1 damage from any attack under normal circumstances. To bypass this, Resistance Down debuffs (such as Ether Res Down), or arts which bypasses attribute resistances (such as Blossom Dance or the Zenith-Cannon's art) must be used.

Sturdy Drakebones are common materials in . They can be obtained from Levitath and Millepods, for 58 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks, or for 5 Material Tickets from the Material Market in . They are one of the required components of X, XV, and XX Magazine Capacity Up augments. Five of them are needed for The Party Line.

Strobe Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Candid & Credible Raygun. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission The Miracle Maker, alongside the Saboteurs Series. The Strobe weapons available in-game are: * Storm Strobe * Soldier Strobe * Warrior Strobe * Ophidian Strobe * Destroyer Strobe * Striker Strobe * Delta Strobe * Original Strobe * Cosmic Strobe * Nebulan Strobe

Swallowtail (Japanese: , Suwarōteiru) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Nia's arts when using Infinity Fans. It can be obtained upon New Game Plus, after finishing the game and installing Patch (Ver.1.3.0). This art recycles Nia's Butterfly Blade.

Sunken Boosters is a DLC Quest in . It is part of the New Quests Pack 4 of the Expansion Pass. It can be received from Borella on the Gwendle Repair Dock in the Kingdom of Uraya. After the completion of this quest, Seesaw can be asked to make more Booster Cylinders at any time. These special salvaging cylinders can only be used at Gormott's Lascham Island, and cause Boosters to be salvaged instead of the usual Collectibles and Treasure items.

Sulala is a NPC in . She is a Nopon who can be found collapsed at Rigitte Harbor in the Leftherian Archipelago during Go for it, Electra!, accompanied by Ookiooki. Ookiooki explains that Sulala was meant to guide her around Leftheria, but got overexcited and hit her head which caused her heart to stop. Ookiooki then requests Electra revive her with her electricity to restart her heart. Doing so requires level 7 "Electric Mastery", and level 3 "Mastery of Thunder".
The Supply Stockpile (Japanese: , Shizai Hokanku) is a Location in . It is located in the City.

Sunny is a NPC in . He is a Nopon from the Nopon Caravans who is found in the Dannagh Desert after the DLC Quest Champion of the Nopon has been accepted. After the quest is completed, he can be found at the Namba Mound Camp. During The Hope of Noponkind, he can briefly be found at the Engardo Pass Camp in High Maktha Wildwood.

Tempest Vangs (Japanese: , Tenpesuto Vanpu) are enemies in . They are members of the Vang family, and can be found at level 75 in Windy Cave on Bionis' Leg. Defeating ten of them is required to complete the quest Nic's Training given by Nopo'rikh in Colony 6. They can drop the Vang Star Wings needed for Colony 6 Reconstruction.

The Telethia Laboratory (Japanese: , Tereshia Kenkyūshitsu) is a location in . It is located in the High Entia Tomb, hidden behind the east wall of the Ceremony Hall. It is guarded by the level 96 Unique Telethia Furious Jozan, which can be avoided for example by using Aerial Cloak gems. The High Entia Emblem is required to gain access to this location, and it is therefore unavailable until after the events of the Mechonis Core. The Telethia Research, needed for the quest Secret Research, can be found here. Lorithia and Alvis have their conversation about the spear used to kill Zanza, who was possessing Arglas' body at the time, on Prison Island, and about Ether here.

Tempestuous Edegia (Japanese: , Ōarashi no Eidejia) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Laia family, and can be found at level 39 on Hovering Reef 10 between the Ether Crystal Deposit and the Ether Plant teleport pad. It must be defeated to complete the Challenge 2 quest in Alcamoth. It can drop a Juicy Laia Fish, three of which are needed for Honouring the Nopon Sage.

Test Pit 2 (Japanese: , Chika Kōdō Dai 2 Shikutsu-ba) is a location in in . It is located in the Ether Mine and can be found by heading south from Test Pit 1, then east at the first fork in the tunnels. It is inhabited by a Junk, Materia, and Rock Krabble. It also contains a Fire Ether Crystal deposit which produces Strength Up II and Bind Resist II crystals. The rank of these crystals increases during Colony 6 Reconstruction when Colony 6's Nature level is increased to level 3 and above. Near the area, another Junk Krabble, three Colony Upas, and two Drunk Vangs can be found.
Teterra Pods (Japanese: , Tetera Poddo) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Pods, and can be found in the Chilkin Lair on Valak Mountain. Teterra Pods release Ent Antols.

The Telethia Galvin (Japanese: , Tereshia no Gangu) is a quest exclusive enemy in . It can be found at level 88 in Revelation Hall in Alcamoth during A Merciful End, where Rozeal asks the party to put Galvin, now a Phoenix-type Telethia, out of his misery. Since this location can only be reached by teleporter, Broken Ether Furnace 2 must be completed first. Telethia Galvin must be defeated to complete A Merciful End. In addition to its normal drops, Telethia Galvin always drops an Armour Shard.

Taos Phoenix Eggs are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are dropped by Taos on Valak Mountain. No one has them available for trade. According to their description, they are gigantic eggs with the yolk on the outside and the white in the middle.

The Telethia Plume (Japanese: テレシア・プルーム, Tereshia Purūmu) is a Nemesis in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a form of the Telethia. It is fought at level 30 beneath the Divine Roost in Noctilum during the Nemesis Squad Mission The Planet's Guardian. It begins with 2,250,000 RP.

no2=THEMEX is a track in Xenoblade Chronicles X, composed and arranged by Hiroyuki Sawano. It is track two of disc one from the XenobladeX Original Soundtrack, and the second part of the suite titled 0rCH-SUITE "X". This music is heard when entering New Los Angeles for the first time, as well as when the Ma-non tow their ship into New Los Angeles at the end of Chapter 5 and when Cross returns from a successful test of the Flight Module in A Girl's Wings. The way is a vocal remix of this song.
Talon Rock Summit (Japanese: , Kagizumeiwa Chōjōbu) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia, above Sayram Lake. It is only accessible via the Flight Module.

Thallium Oc-servs (Japanese: , Tariumu Me-Tsuu) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Oc-serv machines, and can be found at level 43-45 at Badr Stronghold, Hilal Stronghold, Anvil Rock One, Lower Delusian Mountains, above FN Site 412, and Sylvalum Searoad in Sylvalum.

The Tainted Sphinx (Japanese: , Puraedo Ryuosu) is a Main Boss in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Tainted group as a Sphinx variant infected by a virus. It is fought at level 24 at Millstone Ridge in Noctilum during Chapter 6, after the party retrieves the alien mech. Upon its defeat, three more Tainted Sphinxes appear, but before they can attack the party, a flying creature appears and kills them all. After being defeated in the story, a level 30 Tainted Sphinx can be battled at Oblivia's Barbarich Desert in the Time Attack Mission The Infernal Beast.

The Talon Rock Prominence (Japanese: , Kagizumeiwa no Sentan) is a Scenic Viewpoint in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is on the southernmost tip of Primordia's Talon Rock Summit, on which FN Site 110 is also located, and can only be reached by flight. It is uninhabited by day. As with all Scenic Viewpoints, its discovery yields an achievement ("Scaling Talon Rock Prominence").

TP351: Tempera is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be seen in her Skell briefly after defeating the Cross Qmoevas near Noctilum's Everwhelm Falls during the mission Frontier Spirit if the B route option "Assist" is chosen. If the A route option "Encourage" is chosen instead, both Corwin and Raleigh will mention her in conversation after the mission. She is later encountered, battled and definitively defeated during Unknown Assailant.

Tectonic Puges (Japanese: , Kurasuto Berude) are Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Puge machines, Ganglion's human size robots, and are fought at level 40 in Ruined City of O'rrh Sim in Cauldros during The Duel (Part IV). Four of them are fought in the first battle, and three are fought during the second battle. The third battle may include a final group of four tectonic puges, depending on a choice made during the mission.
Synchronicity is a special Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts two Orpheans. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission A Fateful Choice.
T-Claws are back weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from MG062: Megisia or by destroying Galdrs' weapon appendages.

The System Control Room (Japanese: , Shisutemu Seigyoshitsu) is a landmark in . It is located in the Ancient Ship, beyond Fuel Tank #2, and requires an Ether Cylinder to power its mechanism and thus open the door to proceed. This door leads into the Engine Room.

Tattooed Hugo (Japanese: , Shisei no Suparou) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Rhogul family and can be found at level 31 at the Mine Elevator in the Empire of Mor Ardain. It will not appear naturally during Geothermal Haze weather. It must be defeated in order to unlock Zenobia's level 3 "Leaping" Field Skill. Tattooed Hugo is perched atop a tower east of the Mine Elevator. The tower has no ladder, but the top can be reached by riding a cable car from the Beraf Industry Ward power plant in Alba Cavanich. During Geothermal Haze weather, a level 85 Gabondo Lexos patrols the area and will attack if the party is level 92 or less, potentially knocking them off the cable car.

Tevissa is an Ardainian NPC in . She can be found near the Salvage Point on the Goldmouth Flight Deck in the Argentum Trade Guild. If spoken to when Adenine is in the party, she will tell her that Tome of Morytha #3 can be found by salvaging at Umon's Shipyard in the Gormott Province. Tevissa will not appear before Adenine's Lv 2 Affinity node is unlocked, and will disappear permanently once the Tome has been retrieved. She offers no Quests or Merc Missions.

Test of Courage (Japanese: , Kimodameshi) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Gormott Province, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 2 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 50 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 12 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Dark Mastery", "Phonex Linguistics" and "One Lucky Gal" Field Skills.

Taminbi Theft is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Indoline Praetorium from Eliviel at the Seoris Plaza West Gate, when the nation has at least 1 star in Development Level. After Chapter 8, it can also be received automatically from the Leftherian Archipelago; if the mission was already unlocked in Indol before that point, it will be transferred to Leftheria. The time required to complete this mission is 40 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 10 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Info Collector", "Fortitude" and "Agronomy" Field Skills.

This page lists the quests available in Temperantia. The list may be viewed in the order they become available or the order they appear in the Quest Log. Some quests require certain Blades to be acquired or leveled up. Due to the nature of unlocking Blades, it may be difficult to do all of these quests as soon as the chapter requirement is met. If a quest requires a specific Blade, it will be noted. |-|Aux Core = |-|Skill RAM/Upgrade = Telepathy (Japanese: , Ishindenshin) is an Aux Core or a Skill RAM/Upgrade in . It increases the chance that a Blade Art has to be used in response to the Driver's actions by up to 100%. This effect stacks with the Blade Art activation chance boosting effects of Affinity and Trust. The rank II variant allows for 100% activation rate on Critical Up, Accuracy Up, Nullify Reaction, Back Attack Up and Draw Aggro, regardless of Trust level. The rank V variant will guarantee the same for Arts Plus, Recharge Boost, Absorb Damage and Debuff Cancel. The Skill RAM/Upgrade variants can be used to customize Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ as an Aux Core equivalent. _

Takedown Smash (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Zeke's arts when using a Cobra Bardiche. It can be obtained upon New Game Plus, after finishing the game and installing Patch (Ver.1.3.0). This art recycles Zeke's Powerhouse Smash.

Teo is an NPC in . He is an elderly Tornan who can be found in Hyber Village in the Kingdom of Torna, where he runs the inn. He is the estranged husband of Mireille. He is involved during the quest Unforgotten Promise where he must be rescued near Lett Bridge, and his Community is gained alongside Mireille's upon its completion. In the main game of , Teo also briefly appears during the flashback where Lora and Jin check out the house Ornelia lived in. However, his appearance is different than his appearance in , being that of a Tantalese.
Telepathic Bell is a Key Item in . It can be crafted by Addam at Campsites.

Teelan's Laboratory (Japanese: , Teto no Kenkyūjo) is a location in . It is a small building located on the Bionis' Shoulder, used as a base for Teelan and Tyrea's research on Telethia. It is inaccessible until the party saves Teelan in Alcamoth. It is destroyed by Gael'gar in an attempt to put said research to a stop. There is a Pororo's Favourite behind the lab, and no enemies here except during the attack.

Testudos (Japanese: , Tesutudo) are Minor Enemies in . They are Agnian Levnises. They can be found as Quest Exclusive Enemies at level 23 or 47 in the City during Side Story: Sena, are Story Exclusive Enemies at level 50-51 on the Ascension Grounds of Agnus Castle prior to defeating the Queen of Agnus during Chapter 6, and are normal enemies at level ? at Erythia Relay Base in Erythia Sea and level 84-85 at Levnis Workyard in Agnus Castle Barbican. One is also seen during D's past life as Blackblaze Dirk before he became a Moebius. The Testudos in Agnus Castle will not target the party, regardless of the party's level.
Taos Wingtips are items in . They can be dropped by Taos enemies in any rarity (white, yellow, or purple). One of white rarity is needed to craft the Empowered Combo level 2 gem.

Tempapa is a Nopon NPC in . He initially can be found on Daedal Isle in Erythia Sea during Culinary Repertoire, and later during Uniting the Seven Nopon. After Uniting the Seven Nopon, Tempapa can be found in Samon's workshop at the Mxene Tech Quarter in the City. He is one of the Seven Legendary Nopon who wield an Ultimate Hammer.
Tempapa's Memo is a Key Item in . Tempapa gives it to the party for them to deliver it to Samon in the City during Culinary Repertoire.

Thank-You Card is a Key Item in . It is found in the locked room in the Lost Numbers Dormitory in the City that can be opened with the Homecomers' Key after completing the quest The Key to a New Home.
Taleb is an NPC in who can be found in the City. He is the twin brother of Kotan.

Tessa is a NPC in . She is from House Rhodes and is a member of the Lost Numbers who is found at the Memorial Hall in the City after the DLC Quest For the Sake of Keepsakes. She and Jake are married and have been very close for years.
Tatalkin Totems are Normal Enemies in . They are Totems, and can be found at level 42 on the Black Mountains.

Tactics Manual, vol. 5 is an Accessory in . It can be obtained from the Relic on the upper path northeast of the Lakeside Camp. It is accessible via an Ether Slide built on the island below and southwest of Surrogate Fitzpatrick's gravestone, leading to a outcropping above the Lakeside Camp. The Relic can be found by jumping of the east edge.
The Tarnished Ring is a Key Item in . It is found around the Gelgemos Garrison during Regret and Resolve. It is a City soldier's keepsake.

Tactical Action is a track from , composed by Kenji Hiramatsu. It is track four of disc one on the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track four of disc twelve from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. It is a more instrumental version of Tactical Action (Dynamic), and plays whenever the party engages an enemy in battle whenever "Tactical Action (Dynamic)" is the current area theme. These scenarios include: * The battle against Colony Sigma at Everblight Plain. * Between leaving the Forward Post Camp and reaching the Gura Flava Lowlands in Alfeto Valley during Chapter 1. * During Colony Lambda's ambush on the party in the Urayan Tunnels. * Between destroying the Keves Castle Anni

Three Sage Summit (Japanese: , Sandaikenja no Itadaki) is a Secret Area in . It is located on Valak Mountain. Two Glory Slobos can be found here in the daytime and three Gloria Slobos can be found at nighttime. Final Marcus also spawns at the summit at night in clear weather. After the events at Mechonis Core, during a blizzard, Avalanche Abaasy is present at night instead. Several collection orbs can also be found here.

The Missing Partner (Japanese: , Kaettekonai Aibō) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Kurralth, who relocated to the Harict Chapel on Valak Mountain after the Mechonis Core event, but only if Adventurers in Peril was not completed. Completing the quest unlocks the ability to upgrade the party's default Blades, granting them a boost to their stats in their base class, by using Origin Shards that they have collected.

The Unstrung Lute is a Key Item in . It is found just northwest of the Argan Cathedral Ruins on the Black Mountains. The quest A Melody Sustained is accepted upon collecting it. The lute is fixed by Miguel and given to Glimmer, who begins learning how to play the instrument, with A as her tutor.
Valak Slalom is a Nopon Grand Prix Score Attack Course in . It takes place on Valak Mountain at night. This course starts at Zokhed Pass and finishes at the Bionis' Wrist.
V-Beams are back weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from MG062: Megisia or by destroying Galdrs' weapon appendages.

Warning Lamps (Japanese: , Irapuranpu) are collectables in . They can be found on the Fallen Arm. According to their description, they are lamps that shine on low power and they are really fragile so they break easily. Three are required for the reconstruction of Colony 6. In , they can be purchased from the Nopon Archsage in Time Attack for 10,500 Noponstones.

Wandering Amon (Japanese: , Hōrō no Amon) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Eks family, and can be found at level 98 at night near the ether crystal deposit on Bionis' Right Elbow on Valak Mountain.

The Ventilation Conduit (Japanese: , Sōfūki-nai Jankusu-mae) is a landmark in . It is located on the fifth floor of the Central Factory. It can only be accessed when the Junks is flown back to the Central Factory, after the events at the Meyneth Shrine, in order to destroy the Apocrypha Generator.

Vortice, the Deific Blast (Japanese: , Bakunetsu-shin Vorutiche) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Colubrim family and can be found at level 94 above the caldera of Mount M'gando in Cauldros during brimstone rain weather. It is the most powerful enemy in Cauldros. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Vortice, the Deific Blast. During battles with Vortice, the Deific Blast, the boss theme "CR17S19S8" plays instead of the standard Tyrant theme "Uncontrollable".
Visigel Poison Orbs are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from black Visigels. They are components in X, XV, and XX Weapon Attack Power Up and Custom.WP-ATK augments.

The Village Guardian (Japanese: , Omamori-sama) is a landmark in . It is a large statue located on Fonsett Island in the Leftherian Archipelago, just beyond Fonsett Village. It can be moved in order to access the hidden entrance to Spirit Crucible Elpys. There are no enemies here.

The View of a Lost Time (Japanese: , Ushinawareta Toki no Chōbō) is a Secret Area in . It is located in the Streets of the Land of Morytha, at the very top of the Genome Center building. The Level 8 "Earth Mastery" and Level 5 "Superstrength" Field Skills are required to reach this area by toppling a lamppost on Highway 8. The Level 8 "Earth Mastery" and Level 5 "Leaping" are then required to perform a "wall jump" off a ladder. It must be visited to unlock Kasandra's level 5 "Fortune" Battle Skill. The Heart-to-heart "Morytha the Unknown" is located here, as is one Traveling Bard. There are no enemies here.

Vengeful Zadazan (Japanese: , Fukushū no Zadazan) is a quest exclusive Boss in . It is a tank-like weaponized Titan carrying the Nopon Zadazan. It is fought at level 69 at the Island Base Lindwurm in the Leftherian Archipelago during Bana's Revenge.

Vermilion Barks are Tree collectibles in . They can be found in the Kingdom of Uraya, in particular from the Collection Point on the island under the Ruins of Fountain Park. In the , Vermilion Barks can also be obtained by scanning an amiibo.

Warming Stralu is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Tantal from Lucanos at Anastatia's, when the nation has at least 1 star in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 40 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 10 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Dark Mastery" and "Water Mastery" Field Skills.
Vool Ignas (Japanese: , Voraru Igūna) are enemies in . They are members of the Igna family, and can be found at level 31-35 at the Old City of Teddim in the Empire of Mor Ardain.

The Voracious Aspar (Japanese: , Donshoku no Angu) is a quest-exclusive boss in . It is a member of the Aspar family, and can be found at level 60 in the Vault of Heroes in Spirit Crucible Elpys during The Ties That Bind. After a portion of its health has been depleted, it can use "Skin Upgrade", rising its level and fully restoring its HP if it is not defeated fast enough. It is summoned to eat Mamumu's daughter, Mimin, to empower it for a Nopon cult to shape the world as they see fit. But the Aspar goes out of control and swats the cult leader away.
Vorden (Japanese: , Vonvi) is an NPC in . He is a Driver who can be found at the Training Ground in the Kingdom of Uraya during the quest A Test of Strength.

The Victory Contract is a Key Item in . It is received as a reward after completing the Merc Mission The Water City. It enables the purchase of Victory Smoothies from the Café Savvy shop from the Torigoth shop at Torigoth in the Gormott Province.

Wagon Guard is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Leftherian Archipelago, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 4 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 100 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 25 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Expeditionist" and "Transport Mastery" Field Skills. It rewards store contracts that unlock the following wares: * Armu Milk Earl Grey from Cafe Lutino (after relocation to Fonsett). It is needed to finish out Gorg's and Sheba's Affinity Charts.

Volff Tricks is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Empire of Mor Ardain by speaking to Ilmina in the Cargo Transportation Zone, when the nation has 5 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 2 hours, but it can be reduced down to 30 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Ancient Wisdom", "Focus" and "Extra-Ancient Wisdom" Field Skills.

Vessel Scrapping is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Indoline Praetorium by speaking to Nattua at Goetuis Port, when the nation has at least 3 stars in Development Level. After Chapter 8, it can also be received automatically from the Leftherian Archipelago; if the mission was already unlocked in Indol before that point, it will be transferred to Leftheria. The time required to complete this mission is 1 hour, but it can be reduced down to 15 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Focus", "Transport Mastery" and "Industry Mastery" Field Skills.

Vladdy is an Urayan guard in . He is stationed at the Holy Gate of Fontana in Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya. He directs the party to the docks, while also revealing that the availability of ships leaving Uraya depends on the Titan being above the Cloud Sea, and that all direct routes between Uraya and the Empire of Mor Ardain have been severed due to the escalating tensions.

The Viridian Gate (Japanese: , Viridisu-mon, Viridis Gate) is a landmark in . It is located in the northwestern area of Auresco, and serves as a connector between the wards of the city and the Sachsum Gardens. A group of soldiers practice drills here. A Gargoyle is fought here during their attack.
The War Room (Japanese: , Sakusen Shireishitsu) is a Landmark in . It is located in the City.
Virid Park (Japanese: , Wiride Kōen) is a Location in . It is located in the City. The Memorial Hall is located here.
Vinisog Holm (Japanese: , Biningu-tō) is a Location in . It is located in Erythia Sea in the Cadensia Region. The remains of a Leftherian Titan makes up this island.
Voppa Bunnits are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Bunnit family, and can be found at level 88-89 on the Shattered Pathway in The Cavity of Swordmarch.
War of Attrition (Japanese: , Senryaku: Yamakuzushi, Tactic: Mountainbreaker) is a Chain Art in . It is Isurd's Chain Art during a Chain Attack.

Warmount Ignas are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Igna family, and can be found at level 45 at the Argan Cathedral Ruins on the Black Mountains as part of an Enemy Territory. They ride on Rhinons.

Werner (Japanese: , Verunā) is a Homs in . He can be found at the Mechon Wreckage Site in Colony 9, and in the flower gardens of Colony 6. He eventually sets up a shop in Colony 6, selling butterfly biscuits and ribbons.

Wet Rats (Japanese: , Nurerattotto) are collectables in . They can be found on Valak Mountain. According to their description, although they have thick soggy fur, cuddling one keeps someone warm. Five are required for A Gift For Miko.

White Covers (Japanese: , Howaito Kabā) are collectables in . They can be found in Prison Island. According to their description, they are lovely solid white boards and no one wants to know from what they are made.

White Eduardo (Japanese: , Junpaku no Edowarudo) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Brog family, and can be found at level 17 on the island in the middle of Raguel Lake on Bionis' Leg during storms only. Defeating this monster is required for completing the Challenge 1 - Part 1 quest, given near the Refugee Camp. It can drop Brog Leg Meat, which is needed for Material Quest 1.

Whale's Weeper (Japanese: , Kujira no Ruisen) is an Unexplored Territory in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located inside Whale's Gullet in Noctilum. Three level 50 Tyrants appear at night and late night: Seti, the Light of Stars, Sacrum, the Noctilucent and Olegario, the Iron-Helmed. As with all Unexplored Territories, its discovery yields an achievement ("Welcome to Whale's Weeper").

The West Gate (Japanese: , Uesuto Gēto) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Industrial District and connects the city to West Gate Plain. When Cross first arrives in New Los Angeles, this gate is closed. Instead, there is an elevator above the gate available for use.

The Weeping Whitewood (Japanese: , Shidare Hakuju Genseirin) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a glade located in Noctilum, in the mid-upper eastern part of the continent, just inside the walls north of Fukai Pass and northeast of FN Site 215. It can also be reached by following the path from the Ensconced Citadel. Ackwar can be found here during Murder Most Foul. The Scenic Viewpoint Skygazer's Atrium overlooks the wood, but is not directly connected to it.

The White Phosphor Lake (Japanese: , Hakurinko) is a Scenic Viewpoint in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in western Cauldros, north of the Emerian Battlegrounds and surrounding FN Site 503. It is most notably inhabited by several Phosphorous Filiavents and the Tyrant Trueno, the Cataclysm, who guards a teleporter which leads to the small floating mining frigate east of the Far Isle of Tzu'o containing a Level 5 Archaeological Treasure Box with an Extend Overdrive X Augment. The lake itself should not be stepped in, and deals 1200 damage in the same manner as lava. Lulladu can be found here during Gorkwa Games, as can Kiliran during The Old Gods. Weaponized (Japanese: , Nyūsutā, New Star) is a DLC Affinity Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be accepted at Outfitters Test Hangar in the Industrial District.

Wildcat Fortress (Japanese: , Yamaneko no Yōsai) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Ganglion base located in Cauldros, southwest of FN Site 504, in the zone near Cauldros Gate. There is a teleporter here that links to the Forgotten Mining Frigates above the Titan's Table.

White Stabilizers are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from silver Fal-swos that have green lights, or for 90 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components in X, XV and XX Magazine Capacity Up augments.

]] Weather is an environmental effect in and . The types of weather vary by location, with most outdoor areas having three distinct types of weather. Some locations such as Colony 9 are sheltered, and so do not experience changes of weather. Although Alcamoth is also sheltered, its clear dome allows the outside weather to be seen. Most weather types will last a random amount of time up to 12 hours (12 minutes of real time); the exceptions are fair weather and light fog, which have a higher probability and thus can persist for longer periods. The Wastes of Hubris (Japanese: , Fukaki Gyō no Atochi) is a location in . It is located on the Streets of the Land of Morytha, between Great Wall Tunnel No. 8, the Decaying Titan and the Wall Power Control Room. It is a long corridor filled with rubble.

Water Hilns (Japanese: , Wotā Hirun) are enemies in . They are members of the Hiln family, and can be found in the Stomach of the Kingdom of Uraya. In particular, they can be found at level 20-26 in Farlaine Wells and level 24-26 in the Fonsa Myma Waters. Five of them must be defeated to unlock Perceval's level 2 Grim Moon.

Weird Water (Japanese: , Mizu ga Ayashii) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Gormott Province, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 5 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 2 hours, but it can be reduced down to 30 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Botany", "Ichthyology" and "Keen Eye" Field Skills.

Water Quality Check is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Uraya, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 2 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 80 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 20 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Keen Eye", "Water Mastery" and "Info Collector" Field Skills.
Willas is an NPC in . He is a Leftherian who can be found on Fonsett Island in the Leftherian Archipelago. He gives the quest School is in Session.

Wine Delivery (Japanese: , Wain Yusō) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Gormott Province, and is unlocked automatically when Garfont Mercenaries reaches Merc Level 5 and the nation reaches 5 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 2 hours, but it can be reduced down to 30 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Production Mastery", "Electric Mastery" and "Ice Mastery" Field Skills.

White and Cold is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Empire of Mor Ardain, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 4 stars in Development Level. It will only become available after visiting the Kingdom of Tantal for the first time. The time required to complete this mission is 100 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 25 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Production Mastery" and "Fortitude" Field Skills. It rewards store contracts that unlock the following wares: * Steamflake Tabbouleh in Griogair's Greens * Icicle Marimba in Adelno Music

Whisperwind Crossing (Japanese: , Kazanaki no Tsuribashi) is a location in . It is a pair of suspended walkways located on the Bionis' Shoulder, leading from Pillar Knoll to Soltnar Seal Island. No music plays here normally; there is only the sound of wind. There is a Quiet Moment here - "A Life Without Visions" - between Melia and Shulk.
Waterlily is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Lifesage class. When used, it creates a field that heals allies standing within at a rate of 75% of the user's Healing Power every three seconds.
Wellwell's Emporium is a shop in . It is run by Wellwell at Centrilo Parade in the City. Various books required for various quests are sold here.
Wellwell is an NPC in who can be found in the City. He is the owner of Wellwell's Emporium.
White Pippitos are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Pippito family, and can be found at level 45 on Ignia Hill on the Black Mountains during Light Snow.

Yura (Japanese: , Yūrī) is a High Entia in Xenoblade Chronicles. He can be found in Alcamoth on the north side of the central escalator on the ground floor, near the entrance. After the events at the Mechonis Core, he can be found in Harict Chapel in Valak Mountain. If he migrates to Colony 6, he can be found south of the Armu Farm, leaning against the backside of the houses.

Wisps (Japanese: , Ranpusu) are flying enemies in the . They resemble fireflies or wasps, and mainly come out at night. They light up in the night air, making it easier to spot them from a distance. They are similar in size to Skeeters and Fliers. All Wisps have the same appearance.

Worldly Slash (Japanese: , Tenchiken) is one of Dunban's physical arts in . It may decrease the target's Physical Defence by 20%. If used after Gale Slash, it may also inflict Strength Down 20% if all hits connect, reducing the damage dealt by the enemy's physical attacks.

You Can Do It (Japanese: , Ganbaru mo) is one of Riki's support arts in . It has a frontal line range and any ally within the range will be healed, including Riki. Riki's healing power can be further increased depending on the number of debuffs on allies.

Yellow Slobos Rocks are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by three different types of Slobos on top of Three Sage Summit on Valak Mountain, or traded for with Yura before he moves to Colony 6. According to their description, they are stones that enchant all with their light and it is believed that their shine will fade someday. One is needed for Replica Monado 5.

Yoink! (Japanese: , Itadaku mo) is Riki's Talent Art in . It is a physical attack which inflicts damage and steals an item, HP, Strength, Ether, or Agility from an enemy. AP and EXP are added to this list upon unlocking the respective "AP for All!" and "EXP for All!" skills in Riki's Flexibility skill tree.

Young Brogs (Japanese: , Ian Guroggu) are enemies in . They are members of the Brog family, and can be found at level 95 in Tephra Cave, on the second floor, north of the Heavenly Window. Young Brogs are the most powerful Brogs in the game. They are also the only enemies that drop the Diamond Brog Eye needed for Replica Monado 5.

Yama, the Obliviator (Japanese: , Bōkyaku no Yama) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Sylooth and can be found at level 33 north of Tripod Rock in Noctilum. Several Forest Adseculas with group loyalty fly above Yama. It must be defeated during the Squad Mission Buzz, Buzz, Buzz for the BLADE Mission No.6.
Xiphias (Japanese: , Rumederu) are flying swordfish-like creatures in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia, Noctilum, and Sylvalum.
Yggralith (Japanese: , Yegirasu) are extraordinarily powerful draconic Ultrafauna enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. There are only three known Yggralith.

Xair, the Cerulean Walker (Japanese: , Sōten no Eguzēa) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Coronid family. It can be found at level 75 in the southwest Sylvalum Waters. It has an immensely powerful ether-attribute spike which also inflicts Ether Res Down VI.
